claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it ever starts; the lock only protects an execution once it is running.
If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each one runs in turn.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (pipelineType V2).
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` when defining a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ points to the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource documentation, which is described in a later section of the page.
The AWS CodePipeline concepts page (concepts-how-it-works.html) documents pipeline execution modes.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, the run that doesn't get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can be applied to the environment targeted by a deployment job to prevent concurrent runs.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level setting that controls how the stage interacts with an exclusive lock check on an environment it references.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines stage `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time in order.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
An update-conflicts troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/.
A registry API doc page exists at /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` and `args: --yes`.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent builds target the same Pulumi stack, the build that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.

Pulumi Cloud, with a version control integration configured, posts infrastructure-change summaries as pull request comments and status checks, and links each stack update to the commit and pull request that produced it.
Pulumi offers native version control integrations for popular Git hosts, documented at /docs/integrations/version-control/.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes deployments (so Pulumi updates don't overlap).
In Azure Pipelines, the stage-level setting `lockBehavior: sequential` is used together with an exclusive lock check on the environment to make queued runs execute in sequence.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
AWS CodePipeline pipeline has an execution mode setting with value `QUEUED`.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting **Limit the number of simultaneously running builds** to 1 on the build configuration serializes builds so deployments do not overlap.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored 'limit-concurrent-builds' describing this setting.
